description:
At 13 GB, :file.pread into chunk binaries copies the whole file once into BEAM memory (and allocates and frees ~200 refc binaries of 64 MB). The fast native entries mmap the file. The BEAM has no mmap for binaries, but a NIF can expose a mapped file as a binary term with enif_make_resource_binary: the term is an ordinary binary to Elixir (and so to Elixir mode), sub-binaries of it are the chunks, and nothing is copied until the kernel reads it. Keep it outside the kernel subset (an I/O helper, e.g. Defk.IO.mmap/1 or an example-local NIF), with the resource destructor unmapping when the term is collected.

Measure first on the 100M example whether I/O is actually the bottleneck (pread throughput vs kernel throughput per core); if the kernel is slower than the disk, this ticket is not worth doing before the full-size run. That is why it is blocked by the example ticket and needs-triage.

Risks: a page fault inside a kernel is time the safepoint clock sees but ERTS does not; a mapped file that is truncated under the mapping is a SIGBUS, which is a node crash (fault containment, defk-7dm). Both must be stated as limits.

Done when: either the measurement shows I/O is not the bottleneck and this is closed with the numbers, or the helper exists with a test and the 1BRC example can run on it.
title: mmap-backed input binaries for large files
